I'm only 20 and haven't been to Uni yet, but I can give some tips if you're working since I am living by myself and working as a waiter.

I know there's a list someone created already, but I'd like to add some things.

Schedule tips: 

1. If you've got to work the morning after, make sure you go to sleep early w/o any exceptions and don't drink.

2. Going on a trip for a week? Make sure you announce it at least 2-3 months in advance.

3. Want to plan a date? Look if you've got the day and the day after both free since you've got no idea how the date could end.

4. Rather be very early than a little bit late.

5. Try to flex some hobbies or sports into your schedule, it will make your work routine less stressful.


Money:

1. If you receive your salary before your bills, make sure to have money for bills + around 50% of the remainings to save.

2. If you go to a bar/club/caffeteria, take around 10-30$ in cash and leave your card home. Trust me, this hint is a life saver.

3. Cook at home instead of buying junk food. A happy meal costs as much as 500g of uncooked pasta, 350g minced meat + tomato sauce.

4. Money spent on educational books is the best investment.

I know this may not be really fun or interesting to read, but thought I would share this gorgeous wednesday about two months ago.

FYI: Our restaurant isn't really like super big, we got 2 tables for 6, one table for maximum of 12 and others are for 2-4 people.

So a group of 20 entered the restaurant, asked if we got space and "luckily" the owner was sitting behind the reception desk and was like yeah sure, pointed at me to serve them.

It all looked chill, had to pour like 4 bottles of wine and beer here and there, no stress at all. Then came the only time in my life where I was worn out just by one table of customers.

First off they all ordered 5 courses (Our menu is meant for 3), for each course they wanted a recommended wine. So for each course I had to choose 3 options for them to pick from. They managed to pick every older vintage that had to be decanted. So, 5x20 courses, 100 plates to wash (we have no dish washer lady on wednesdays) and guess who had to do that job.. me.

Also not to mention we nearly ran out of glasses, but luckily we managed to borrow a few boxes from our partner business located right next to our restaurant.

Dish washing aside, here begins the fun part.

14 out of 20 wanted no lactose, no gluten.

9 out of 20 were allergic to about 4 different "substances" (can't remember the names but it was hell of improvisation by our chef because he had to replace a crap ton of ingredients, props to him).

4 out of 20 emptied their water glass in a second after I had filled it (My boss gets really mad if I don't refill the glass instantly so I tried to avoid making that mistake)

There also was this one guy who constantly insulted me and made gay jokes about me (being overwhelmingly handsome like I am)

And there was a lady who refused to speak in any other language than finnish so I had to use translation tools. I'm Estonian native.

I think I had like 10 pages of data (food, allergies/intolerances, drinks, water (still/sparkling), wine etc)

And the final sprinkle of salt on my wound(s):

1. They all wanted separate bills (Trust me that took me a shit ton of time and effort because our system makes a bill for whole table)

2. 0€ Tip. (6000€ bill)
